articles.summary: Ten years after the UK introduced its opt-out collective actions regime, the Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) has a considerable body of case law to draw on. More than 50 collective actions have been brought and various judgments, settlements and failed claims are beginning to show where the regime works and where its limits lie.
articles.title: Ten years of the CAT: What comes next for collective actions in the UK

articles.summary: As law firms invest more heavily in AI and technology, those investments are reshaping their capital needs, pricing models and the economics of the billable hour. Speaking to SaaSTake, Burford Vice Chair David Perla says, “AI is going to make law firms more capital-intensive at precisely the moment it has the potential to make them more efficient,” as firms consider how to share the benefits of AI-driven efficiency with clients. Learn more.
articles.title: AI and the business of law: David Perla on changing law firm economics
